- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–2%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in the following 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment-driven sell-off.
- Model tends to overpredict early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–7) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias to first 5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags in adjusting; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to align with sentiment pivot.
- Mean reversion is stronger in the last 10–15 days of forecast; if model shows persistent upward trend beyond that, reduce slope by 10–20% to reflect diminishing momentum.
